ai.description: *Calotes zolaiking* reaches a snout-vent length of 85 mm. It is characterized by a vibrant orange-red head and throat, a dark brown body with pale crossbars, and a prominent, serrated dorsal crest.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Calotes zolaiking* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, black-bordered white or yellow stripe extending from the eye to the corner of the mouth.
ai.habitat: *Calotes zolaiking* inhabits the high-altitude subtropical broadleaf forests of Mizoram, typically found at elevations ranging from 1,000 to 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: *Calotes zolaiking* is primarily diurnal and displays a unique defensive strategy by remaining motionless to blend into its surroundings when threatened.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Calotes zolaiking* is oviparous, laying a clutch of 5–9 eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, typically from May to August in Mizoram, India.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Calotes zolaiking* is endemic to the high-altitude forests of Mizoram in Northeast India, specifically occurring at elevations between 1,000 and 1,500 meters.
